plan.correctness_analysis_by_orchestrator: tau_k_run (the 256th largest seen so far) is MONOTONICALLY NON-DECREASING because the 256th order statistic of a superset is >= that of a subset. Therefore a block whose max is BELOW tau_k_run cannot contribute to the global top-256. THE PRUNE CONDITION MUST BE STRICT '<', NOT '<=': a block with max == tau_k_run may hold elements equal to the final threshold, and dropping them corrupts n_eq and hence the D-TIE graded criterion and tau_p/L.
plan.mandatory_precondition_STRENGTHENED: offline study must measure BOTH (a) the pruning rate per case AND (b) the Sort-vs-online-softmax cost split inside one K1 block. (b) is the binding ceiling: online softmax (reduce_max+exp+reduce_sum over BV) must still run on EVERY block, so only the topk+merge portion is saveable. If Sort is a small share of per-block cost, #2 cannot reach 3% no matter how high the pruning rate is. Report the ceiling BEFORE writing any kernel code.

Under i.i.d. logits a whole 4096-element block essentially never falls entirely below the running 256th-largest. Analytical expectation is seed-independent and needs V >~ 1e6 to become material; the contract's max V is 152377.

plan.name: K2g int32 And 'halving' workaround -> 2*BV over-allocation
plan.mechanism: int32 AscendC::And/Or are int16-only, so TileLang int32 bitwise_and consumes count as int16 and processes only count/2 int32 elements. Workaround: state_ub/h_ub/tmp_ub are over-allocated to int32[2*BV] with real data in [0:BV), and count=2*BV so the halved pass covers all BV int32.
plan.cost: TWO wastes, not one: (a) MEMORY 3 buffers x 2*BV x 4B = 24*BV instead of 12*BV -> 12*BV = 49152 B wasted at BV=4096 (33% of K2g's 148452 B); (b) COMPUTE every And executes at 2x element count. lowbias32 = 3 rounds of [xor-shift, multiply] and XOR is emulated as x+t-2*(x&t), so 3 Ands per element at 2x count.
plan.constraints_noted_in_code: int32 xor/not don't compile; scalar-and unregistered. So removing the And is not trivial -- needs an alternative full-count int32 bitwise path (e.g. split into 2x int16 halves, or replace bitwise ops with compare/select arithmetic).
